articles.title: Business sentiment in Aldmark improves on strong chip and cosmetics exports
articles.description: Business sentiment in Aldmark improved for the coming quarter on robust exports of chips and cosmetics, a chamber survey showed.
articles.content:
Business sentiment in Aldmark improved for the fourth quarter on the back of strong semiconductor and cosmetics exports, a survey showed on Sunday.
The business survey index compiled by the Aldmark Chamber of Commerce rose to 94 from 88 in the previous quarter.
A reading below 100 means more companies expect conditions to worsen than to improve.
Chipmakers and cosmetics exporters reported the most optimism, while steel and chemical firms remained cautious.
Large exporters were more upbeat than smaller domestic-focused businesses.
The chamber said weak consumer spending at home and higher shipping costs were the main concerns.

articles.title: Tee plans: enthusiasts draw up blueprint for an 18-hole golf course in the Tarn Highlands
articles.description: The group hopes to put the Tarn Highlands on the regional golf map, with visitors flying in to play a course set among mountain lakes.
articles.content:
A group of amateur golfers has drawn up plans for an 18-hole course in the Tarn Highlands, a region better known for trekking than for sport.
The proposed site sits on a plateau above Lake Orrin, about two hours by road from the regional capital.
The group has asked the provincial tourism board for a long-term lease on the land.
Organisers say the course would be designed to follow the natural slopes and would use rainwater collected in holding ponds.
They hope to attract visiting golfers from neighbouring countries during the dry season.
Local officials have welcomed the idea but said an environmental review would be needed first.
The group plans to host a small nine-hole tournament on a temporary layout next spring to test interest.

articles.title: How regional property markets are drawing fresh capital despite rate uncertainty
articles.description: Three coastal cities emerge as key targets as investors adjust to a higher-rate environment, analysts say.
articles.content:
Property investors are putting fresh money into offices and logistics warehouses in three coastal cities, according to a report released on Friday.
Deal volumes in the region rose by about a fifth in the third quarter from a year earlier.
Analysts said buyers were betting that borrowing costs had peaked.
Logistics assets drew the most interest because online retail keeps expanding.
Office deals were concentrated in newer buildings with lower energy costs.
